issue.title: sase stitch create pushes auto-rebased commits without checking the combined tree, so rename/import semantic conflicts land on master
issue.description:
`sase stitch create` (git/GitHub `create_commit`) runs this sequence: `git commit` -> `_sync_with_origin_after_commit` (fetch, then `git rebase --autostash origin/<default>`, with automatic semantic-conflict resolution) -> `_push_current_branch_with_rebase_retry`, which on rejection fetches, rebases again, and retries. Every step lives in src/sase/vcs_provider/plugins/_git_commit_dispatch.py. The before-commit hook (`just fix`) runs before the commit, and therefore before any rebase. Nothing checks the combined tree that is actually pushed. A clean textual rebase of two independently correct commits can therefore publish a tree that fails to import, as described in the repro field.

ROOT CAUSE: this is a missing gate, not a flaky one. Whenever the rebase moves the base (upstream commits get replayed under the local commit), the pushed tree has never been verified. The Master Gate runs only after the push, so CI detects the break once it is already live.

DIRECTION FOR THE PLANNER (not a prescription):
- When a rebase in create_commit, including the push-retry loop, actually moved the base, run a fast, bounded semantic check on the rebased tree before `git push`. Candidate checks:
  - mypy scoped to files changed by the local commit and by the incoming upstream commits. mypy reported all 5 errors in this incident; whole-repo mypy took 52s inside `sase tool run check`.
  - An AST from-import resolver over the changed modules. A throwaway version that walks every `from sase... import X` in src/ at any depth, including function-local and TYPE_CHECKING imports, and resolves each name with importlib checked 54k names in about 60s. It flagged exactly the 5 bad imports plus 7 TYPE_CHECKING-only aliases, which need allowlisting.
- If the check fails, do not push. Leave the commit local and exit with an actionable message, as the rebase-conflict path does (exit 2 plus a `--resume` flow), so the landing agent repairs the semantic conflict instead of breaking master.
- Keep host capacity in mind (the two-speed CI and check-full-is-explicit decisions). The gate should cost seconds, run only when the base moved, and never grow into a full `just check`.

task_type_fields.impact:
Master stays broken until a human notices. Here `sase tui` crashed at startup for about 35 minutes of live work, and every TUI test shard failed at collection, which masked the unrelated red items behind it. A second, runtime-only break (the Tools pane open-log action always failing with "Could not read log") would not have shown up at startup at all.

The class keeps coming back, and each earlier instance was fixed only at the point:
- sase-lg: c1970b5a0 privatization vs 4d36d6d3d, ImportError on master.
- sase-183: 9bd351b67 used pre-rename fields, mypy failure.
- sase-1b7: a benchmark re-exported a test renamed by sase-19x.9.
task_type_fields.repro:
Pattern: commit A renames or privatizes a symbol (`X` -> `_X`) and updates every caller; commit B, authored on a base without A, adds a new `from mod import X` in a different file. When B lands through `sase stitch create`, `git rebase --autostash origin/master` replays B onto A without a textual conflict (the two commits touch different files), and the rebased tree is pushed.

Concrete instance on 2026-09-28:
1. 31709195f3 (bbugyi200.apollo.2v, committed 20:26:37Z) privatized RowIdentity, ToolRunGlanceSnapshot, ToolRunLogTail, and ToolRunStateStyle to clear the closed sase-1bt `--epic-symbol` whitelist.
2. 386d383a94 (bbugyi200.athena.sase-1bt.land, authored 20:20:01Z, rebased and committed 20:31:57Z) added annotation-only imports of the same four names in loader.py, links_suffixes.py, and tool_runs_pane_tool_actions.py, fixing the same symvision finding the other way.
3. After the clean rebase and push, master fails immediately: `.venv/bin/python -c 'from sase.ace.tui import AceApp'` raises `ImportError: cannot import name 'RowIdentity' from 'sase.ace.tui.tool_runs.attribution'`. Master Gate run 36479869059 failed on mypy (5 attr-defined errors) and on every test shard, where the tests/ace/tui/conftest.py import fails.

Fixed at the point by 9f67a91bce, which dropped the four redundant references and kept the privatization.

issue.creation_reason: Master broke again from a clean auto-rebase of two independently correct commits (sase tui ImportError, point-fixed by 9f67a91bce). This is the fourth instance of the class after sase-lg, sase-183, and sase-1b7; each was fixed only at the point, never in the landing path.
